adopter_notes: Inputs are original synthetic immutable records, public source metadata, operation/attempt identities, and event/availability clocks. Another application must declare what accepted, completed, failed and pending mean, expose permitted readers and supply independently established outcomes. Authorized local source access, Python3.12 with pinned dependencies and Docker are needed for this implementation; model execution additionally uses the already-installed Ollama0.33.3 and pinned Qwen3 model. No-account fixture and fixed-rule checks need no model. Historical replay additionally needs its saved local captures; the public site alone cannot reproduce private source execution. One synthetic Java application was tested, with no universal adapter or outside adoption proof. In the original stopped scope segment, 35 returned generations reported 228,139 input tokens, 19,118 output tokens and 1,207.174618 seconds of generation time. These are known-only subtotals; complete token and generation-time totals remain unknown because one request timed out. Total adapter request time and the conservative parent elapsed clock are shown separately. No account-wide charge or dollar saving is inferred.
completion_policy:
Public investigation-completeness-v1 is a new bounded workflow policy, separate from proposal format, claim support and independent diagnostic grading.
For an unknown outcome, first obtain a complete permitted source inventory. Account for each visible logs, traces and status source. These three kinds define this policy's bounded outcome-reading obligations, not every possible place an outcome could appear. Metrics, changes and pipeline sources create no mandatory reads.
A logs or traces check requests this operation over the complete incident start..cutoff window with limit 1..32. A status check requests this operation as_of cutoff. The status reader returns only its latest observed snapshot; this is not a complete status history. A valid full request with a complete empty or record-bearing response accounts for that reader's bounded check. Narrow, truncated, invalid or wrong-scope reads do not. Do not combine arbitrary partial pages to claim full coverage.
Known unavailable, denied, uncollected, out-of-retention or not-yet-available evidence is an access limit, not an empty read. Returned collection and retention boundaries can limit the window even when truncated is false. Fully blocked public inventory metadata may establish an access limit without a useless read. Partial collection or retention still requires checking the available portion through a full scoped request. Partial or missing inventory cannot establish that all sources were accounted for.
An existing adapter-and-claim-checker-accepted known outcome may stop without reading every source. An unknown proposal may also complete this procedure when legitimate returned observations for this operation and cutoff establish both completed and failed terminal outcomes. That conflict exception does not require a schema-valid unknown proposal, but the proposal must still pass the separate validators before workflow success. Either exception can use a legitimate returned witness from any source kind.
Otherwise, account for all declared obligations. A later valid complete read can finish an earlier partial check; earlier attempts remain recorded. Access or actual execution limits leave a separate limited workflow result. Model claims about exhausted budgets are not trusted counters. A next_check is only a suggestion, never a read. The model chooses every evidence request and its own answer; the host does not prefetch, repair answers or prescribe a diagnosis.
Completion means this finite public procedure was satisfied. It does not prove that all possible evidence exists here, that every returned fact was understood, or that the diagnosis is correct.
current_explanation: Read acquisition, latest native format, retained canonical structure, supported claims, public procedure completion and independent requirements remain separate. An earlier retained canonical proposal is not proof that the final native submission was accepted. The unattempted Java original/reduced/restored slots concern replay of existing real captures, not a fresh Java run. Original failures permanently keep this linked version from meeting its all-20 qualification. In the one new attempted investigation, the model requested inventory and read logs. Exact sanitized excerpt from the third generation native arguments (other fields omitted): {"operation":"archive-job-2"}. That undeclared extra field caused adapter rejection before the claim checker; the checker was not attempted for that submission. The existing public allowlist omits undeclared fields from displayed structures; this labeled excerpt explains the actual invalid input. The original private proposal and every saved verdict remain unchanged. An authorized revision request was dispatched; it produced no valid revised submission. Exact fourth native message: {"role":"assistant","content":""}. It contains zero tool calls and is not a final answer or model abstention. The saved feedback-delivered and delivery-unknown flags remain as recorded; dispatch does not relabel them. The public completion verdict access_limited and the independent required-observations-read flag answer different questions; neither grants workflow success. The native action error stopped the pass with ten follow-up slots unattempted, including all saved Java views.

fresh_java.reason: Original failed attempts keep all-20 qualification closed; no fresh Java was authorized.

partial_usage.note: Known subtotals cover both segments, including unscored setup/mechanics; a partially reported call contributes only its observed components. Unknown generations lack input or output usage. Complete totals remain null. Reserved bounds cover only new missing-usage calls with saved quiescence and fresh-instance recovery; the historical 7172/8192 bounds are excluded from these reservations. Input counts may include repeated input/cache effects; runtime output includes private thinking without a separately observed split. These are not elapsed-compute, electricity or dollar measurements.

related_work: The existing project methods acknowledge observability, bounded tool use, evidence reduction and diagnostic regression work. This implementation contributes an inspectable local experiment and strict host boundaries with measured failures; it does not claim globally unique invention.
reproduction: A clean source-only export of 201 files reused the installed pinned Python dependencies. Checked package imports resolved into the export. This is same-machine reproduction, not outside human verification. The private derivation helper reads closed saved observations only; it does not run or rescore an investigation.
review_note: A separate read-only automated review inspected actual source, frozen identities, tests, the offline scope audit, setup, completed model records, timeout, cleanup and accounting. It confirmed the retained-versus-latest proposal distinction and unknown usage. This was not outside human validation.
scope_correction: Aggregate operation readers may return records from multiple services. A source label is descriptive; an explicit service predicate still restricts records. Source identity, operation, event/availability, permissions, request pairing, payload hashes and record identities remain independently checked. Malformed public responses cannot establish early completion. The opt-in rule leaves legacy interpretation unchanged. Offline replay changes only trace-a coverage in reduced Java: A query q004 and E query q003, at submissions 1 and 2 and final assessment. No overall completion judgment changes. E still leaves log-order and log-worker unread at its final assessment.

scope_impact.note: All89 actual legacy submission/final verdicts matched. Four submission and two final source-coverage verdicts change; no overall completion status or reason changes. One failed trial has no completion verdict. Non-exhausted counter magnitudes in this pure offline audit are placeholders for saved zero/nonzero predicates, not historical measured clocks. No evaluator or model ran; no different model behavior is inferred.

terminal_audit: The old schema already allowed unresolved and failed unknown answers. Two historical final E submissions nevertheless combined resolved with unknown; three earlier first submissions did too before revising. Those failures remain unchanged. Removing a redundant field choice is an interface result, not proof of better reasoning. In the original stopped scope segment, the model selected eight known-outcome actions, all canonically encoded, and three unresolved actions, all rejected for supplying the forbidden outcome field. Four encoded submissions passed the claim checker; four did not. Three representation errors are interface failures, not accepted uncertainty. Seven trials retained a schema-valid canonical proposal, but only five had a schema-valid latest native terminal action. First proposals and later errors remain separate. The source and template were not changed after evaluation began. Separately, the timeout follow-up added one known-outcome action. Its undeclared operation field caused adapter rejection before the claim checker was attempted.
terminal_design: The model selects submit_known_outcome and supplies its outcome, or selects submit_unresolved or submit_investigation_failure. The host encodes respectively resolved plus that supplied outcome, unresolved/unknown, or failed/unknown. All other required content stays model-authored. Forbidden representation fields, bad citations and unsupported claims remain rejected; no legacy answer is silently converted.
tests: 1183 passed in327.59seconds in one coherent clean-source suite; no skips or failures.
timeout_explanation: The original ninth trial reached its 300-second client deadline. Its later containment classification failed; the exact global stop and all nine attempts remain unchanged. The new version records transport timeout evidence before cleanup and permits only proven owned-runtime shutdown followed by a fresh verified instance to end that trial locally. It never retries the timed-out trial. One deliberately interrupted unrelated synthetic mechanics request is unscored and is included in follow-up accounting even though the setup presentation list is empty. Only the eleven original unattempted slots are eligible here. Segment count denominators are the nine retained attempts and eleven replacement slots; the historical execution still contains its original twenty-slot plan and eleven unattempted rows. The linked twenty is a derived view, not an uninterrupted run. Runtime restart changes model loading/cache state, so timing is not a controlled warm-cache comparison. Opaque runtime identities identify saved process observations, not public processes or endpoints.

timeout_observations.reason: Historical timeout remains globally stopped. Its saved input-admission/configuration bounds are not measured processing usage or a retrospective reservation/containment proof.
Contained local timeout; worker/client cleanup, runtime quiescence and a fresh verified instance were saved. This trial did not resume.
